## The claim, stated carefully

There is a tempting sentence:

> Everything is the same model.

In BEDC, the careful version is narrower and stronger:

> Everything that can be licitly spoken, observed, compared, proved, exported, or named inside BEDC must enter through the same model form.

That does **not** mean that music is light, light is number, number is proof, or proof is physical space. It means that once any of them becomes a public BEDC interface, it must be carried by the same kind of certificate grammar.

The shared grammar is:

```text
Hist -> Cont -> Ask -> Sig -> Pkg -> Gap -> NameCert
```

The content differs. The admission route is the same.

## What "speakable" means

A target `X` is BEDC-speakable only when public use of `X` factors through an upward interface:

```text
X^up = (Source, Pattern, Classifier, Stability, Ledger)
```

The source says where the material comes from. The pattern says what repeated or generated form is being read. The classifier says how same and different are judged. The stability row says the reading survives the relevant transports. The ledger says what was compressed, projected, hidden, identified, or left outside the claim.

Only after those rows exist may `X` be consumed as a public name.

```{=html}
<span class="elim-mark">✗ "The thing exists first, then BEDC gives it a name"</span>
```

No. BEDC does not begin with the mature object as a primitive. It begins with generated distinctions and grants a name only when the source, pattern, classifier, stability, and ledger rows license that name.

## The shared model form

The model form of a speakable interface is the role pattern:

```text
ModelForm(X) =
  Hist_X
  hsame_X
  Cont_X
  Ask_X
  Sig_X
  sameSig_X
  Pkg_X
  Gap_X
  NameCert_X
```

This says that a public object is not just a carrier. It is a carrier together with a history source, an internal sameness relation, a continuation route, a probe or asking interface, signature readback, signature comparison, package rows, residue ledger, and naming certificate.

The exact source material can vary completely. A theorem instance, a tensor classifier, a musical phrase, a spectral reading, and a physical-observation packet can have different content while still using this same role pattern.

## Examples

**A number** is not imported as a host natural number. It is read through a generated history pattern, successor or recurrence behavior, induction or recursion ledger, classifier stability, and NameCert.

**A proof** is not imported as a host proof object. It is read through statement rows, dependency rows, proof-flow recognition, certificate rows, status rows, and a theorem-facing NameCert.

**A tensor feature** is not accepted because a probe found a direction. The direction supports a pattern row. It becomes an auditable explanation only when model source, activation protocol, classifier behavior, stability, and ledger rows are sealed by a Tensor NameCert.

**A color reading** is not the physical object. It is a signature generated by an observation protocol. It can support a public object only when the source, probe route, classifier, stability, and ledger rows are visible.

**A musical structure** is not its frequency spectrum. The spectrum is one signature produced by one probe. The musical object needs the history, pattern, classifier, stability, and ledger that make that signature part of a public interface.

The point is not that these are secretly the same object. The point is that none of them gets a public BEDC name by bypassing the certificate form.

## Same form is not identity

Two interfaces can preserve the same BEDC model form without becoming the same thing.

```text
ModelForm(Music) ~= ModelForm(Light)
```

does not mean:

```text
Music = Light
```

It means that the public readings of both must expose comparable roles: source, continuation, signature, package, ledger, and NameCert. The comparison is structural. It is not host-level equality and it is not content collapse.

```{=html}
<span class="elim-mark">✗ "If two things share the BEDC form, BEDC identifies them"</span>
```

No. BEDC keeps identities. It lets operations pass through internal transports such as `hsame`, `sameSig`, and classifier-preserving comparison. It does not collapse distinct sources, patterns, scopes, or ledger residues into one host object.

## Projection is not ontology

This boundary matters most when a projection looks convincing.

A spectrum is not the light. A waveform is not the music. A vector direction is not the learned concept. A theorem identifier is not the proof. A bitstream is not the event flow. A semantic label is not the classifier.

Each can be a useful signature. None is automatically the target whose interface it supports. To make that reading legitimate, BEDC demands a recovery, exactness, or residue ledger explaining what the projection preserved and what it lost.

The slogan is:

> A projection becomes public data only when its missing source is ledgered.

## The compact formulation

The clean BEDC sentence is:

> Everything licitly speakable is a NameCert-licensed projection of distinction-history.

Or, expanded:

> Every public BEDC object is a generated distinction history read through continuation, probe, signature, package, ledger, and naming certificate.

This is a unification claim about admissible structure. It is not a claim that BEDC has reconstructed all mature mathematics, all physics, or all experience. It says what form a claim must take before BEDC allows it to be spoken.

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">💡 Discovery</span>
```

The discovery is that "object" is too late in the story. By the time BEDC can say `X`, the work has already happened: a history was generated, a continuation route stabilized, a signature was read, a package was formed, a gap was ledgered, and a NameCert licensed the public name.
